change: From R0 remove every dot with Euclidean catalogue distance <=3 px; refill the same number from the original H19-5 binary support at distance >3 px in the parent's recorded geodesic BFS visitation order, while preserving the original 2.8 px inhibition rule.
hypothesis: The 0-300 m catalogue collar contains recoverable new-fault truth. Moving R0's collar dots to more distant H19-5 support at fixed mass will therefore cause a small live loss rather than continue the gains obtained by earlier pruning without refill.
mechanism: Known catalogue pixels are masked, but new-fault truth may occur within the 300 m kernel radius of known traces. Count is fixed, so the edit changes only kernel credit and self-credit, not emitted mass. The refill uses no new geological score or hidden-label information.
non_fault_mimic: Catalogue generalization/rasterization can displace a mapped line from its real trace; alluvial channels and map-edge/BFS artifacts inside the binary H19-5 support can mimic fault lineaments during refill.
falsifier: A same-entity receipt increase of at least +0.01 DTI over R0 falsifies the predicted small-loss mechanism. A decrease of at least 0.01 supports it; a smaller absolute change is no evidence because only public chunks are observed.

excluded_variants.PRUNE_1: R0 already has no dots <=1 px, so the specified fixed-count edit is an exact repeat.
excluded_variants.PRUNE_2: R0 is itself the <=2 px prune, so the specified fixed-count edit is an exact repeat.
excluded_variants.MASS: H19-5 is binary at every R0 dot and D2.8/R0 thinning is score-blind; no non-degenerate parent ranking is stored.
excluded_variants.SNAP: The non-PRUNE >=3 px rule conflicts with R0's >2 px construction: 30 dots have no destination simultaneously within 2 px and >=3 px from the catalogue. Resolving them would add a second axis.
